Criterion: tokens/USD saved against the no-op or direct arm; correctness only as zero Edit exact-match failures. The authors state no success threshold for a configuration, so quality and cost verdicts for every entry: no criterion stated by the authors (the authors' own judgements are quoted). Agents: Claude Code + Claude Sonnet; Codex + GPT-5 (model versions Not stated).
- Tool-schema filtering + Claude Code + Sonnet (MCP attached): 392,000 tokens saved over a jinja2 session (~32K/request x 12); 1,220,000 over a 34-request rich session; ~21K/turn fixed (29K -> 8K); cancels ~17K/turn 'proxy tax'; $0.043 vs $0.057 direct on a Sonnet edit task. Quality not measured; authors: 'the only lever that is unambiguously and reproducibly positive'
- Tool-schema filtering + Codex + GPT-5: saves 128-256 tokens; without a core-tool whitelist the agent is paralysed, with it runs commands every turn. Quality not measured (qualitative)
- Content compression + Claude Code + Sonnet (turn-aligned): ~1.5-2K tokens/turn (~2% of cache-priced prefix); 5-turn session cumulative 83,710 tokens (22.2%); whole-task runs dominated by turn count ($0.638/18 turns vs $0.230/7 uncompressed, local backend; $0.268/10 vs $0.469/16, GPU). Zero Edit exact-match failures after the boundary fix; authors: positive only on long sessions with few recalls
- Content compression with recalls (sparkline change): 2 recalls, each costing one compressed segment; recall-free change (max_retries=-1): ~6.5% fewer input tokens, dollar-neutral
- Content compression without recall tool (ablation): 46 turns / $1.85, 3.2x the cost with recall; authors: 'far worse'
- History summarization: not quantified (value is capacity, not dollars); quality and cost not measured
- Paritok-4B compressor, single-shot SWE-bench Lite: 86.5% of uncompressed solve quality retained at 25.7% compression rate (gpt-4.1-mini 85.6% at 50.2%; gpt-5 93.6% at 61.9%); agent tokens/USD not measured; authors say it is orthogonal to multi-turn cost
fields.why: Round 2 gave works/partly/does-not-work verdicts by its own judgement; the rule of 2026-11-23 allows verdicts only on a success criterion stated by the authors, and the paper gives none (it reports savings against the no-op arm and its own qualitative judgements). Verdicts replaced by 'no criterion stated by the authors'; values re-checked against pp. 3-8.

fields.v: Controlled A/B runs on real repositories: compress vs no-op for content (tool filter held fixed), filter on vs off, MCP block pinned with --strict-mcp-config; 2 agent families; 5-turn cumulative experiment in one --resume session. Baseline: no-op arm / direct no-proxy connection. Held constant: agent, model, task, other levers. Acceptance tests: none (Edit exact-match failures only). Repetitions: '>= 3 trials per arm' recommended/stated; exact counts Not stated. Human intervention: Not stated

Tool filtering dominates per session (20:1 to 33:1 vs content compression saving) and is the only reliably positive lever; content compression ~2%/turn but cumulative quadratic, overtaking the tool filter near N ≈ 6 and capped by the ~200K window around turn 12-15; each recall costs one compressed segment; removing recall costs 3.2x. Significance: not tested (no statistics); turn-count variance (7-18 turns) larger than the compression effect

Partly: isolated per-lever savings were distinguishable; whole-task compress vs no-op comparisons reversed sign between runs (variance-dominated). Authors: 'conclusions drawn from one run repeatedly reversed themselves'; only distributions over >= 3 runs trustworthy. Limitations stated: quadratic fit rests on five turns; MCP tool-block jitter; one compressor, two agents

Specific 4B compressor, two agent families, Python-heavy repos; constants will not generalise; quadratic fit on five turns; cap depends on window size and client compaction; Codex-on-Windows shell-encoding noise. Future: symbol map / directed retrieval instead of body deletion

Gateway, 4B model and evaluation harness open source (Apache 2.0, github.com/Paritok-official/paritok-4b-v1). No pre-registration. Language: Python repositories. Authors work for the vendor of the gateway evaluated. Number of runs per configuration and number of tasks not reported; no statistics. Some inconsistency in the headline end-to-end saving: '~25% on a single turn and ~39% by turn five' (p. 2) vs 22.2% cumulative at N=5 in Table 3 (p. 5). Compression ratio reported inconsistently: segment ratio ≈ 0.44 on line-numbered reads (p. 3) vs '∼26% of its size' (p. 3) and 25.7% rate (Table 4). Equation (1) and Fig. 1 garbled in text extraction
